questions.title: Find and interpret a gradient function
questions.prompt_html:
A curve is defined by \(y=2 x^{3} - 4 x^{2} + 4 x - 2\).

Find \(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}\).
questions.solution_html:
Differentiate the cubic, square and linear terms separately. They give \(6 x^{2}\), \(- 8 x\) and \(4\). The constant term has derivative zero.

Answer: \(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}=2 \left(3 x^{2} - 4 x + 2\right)\).
questions.hint_html: Differentiate before substituting. The derivative, rather than the height, describes the gradient.

questions.title: Find and interpret a gradient function

Differentiate the cubic, square and linear terms separately. They give \(12 x^{2}\), \(- 4 x\) and \(-4\). The constant term has derivative zero.

Answer: \(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}=4 \left(3 x^{2} - x - 1\right)\).
questions.hint_html: Differentiate before substituting. The derivative, rather than the height, describes the gradient.

questions.title: Find and interpret a gradient function
questions.prompt_html:
A curve is defined by \(y=8 \sqrt{x} - 4 x - 3 + \frac{3}{x}\). Take \(x>0\).

Find the exact gradient when \(x=4\).
questions.solution_html:
Differentiate first to obtain \(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}=\frac{- 4 x^{\frac{5}{2}} - 3 \sqrt{x} + 4 x^{2}}{x^{\frac{5}{2}}}\).

At \(x=4\), substitute this input into the derivative to give \(- \frac{35}{16}\).

Answer: \(- \frac{35}{16}\).
questions.hint_html: Differentiate before substituting. The derivative, rather than the height, describes the gradient.

At \(x=-1\), substitute this input into the derivative to give \(-4\).

(c)

The gradient at the point is \(-4\). The curve is falling there.

A curve is defined by \(y=4 x^{3} + 4 x - 5\).

  1. Find \(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}\).

    [2]

  2. Find the exact gradient when \(x=-2\).

    [2]

  3. Explain what the sign of your gradient says about the curve at that point.

    [1]
questions.answer_html:
(a) \(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}=4 \left(3 x^{2} + 1\right)\)

(b) \(52\)

(c) The curve is rising there.
questions.solution_html:
(a)

The power term \(4 x^{3}\) gives \(12 x^{2}\). The linear term gives \(4\), while the constant contributes zero.

Answer: \(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}=4 \left(3 x^{2} + 1\right)\).

(b)

Differentiate first to obtain \(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}=4 \left(3 x^{2} + 1\right)\).

At \(x=-2\), substitute this input into the derivative to give \(52\).

Answer: \(52\).

(c)

The gradient at the point is \(52\). The curve is rising there.
questions.hint_html: Differentiate before substituting. The derivative, rather than the height, describes the gradient.

marking_criteria.description_html: Use the power rule term by term.
Find the derivative, then substitute the stated input.
Use the sign of the evaluated derivative to describe the tangent.

questions.title: Differentiate an outer power with an inner function
questions.prompt_html:
The function is \(f(x)=3 \left(4 x + 3\right)^{3}\).

Find \(f^{\prime}(x)\).
questions.solution_html:
Set \(u=4 x + 3\). Its derivative is \(\frac{\mathrm du}{\mathrm dx}=4\).

Use the outer rule for \(f=3 u^{3}\) to get \(\frac{\mathrm df}{\mathrm du}=9 u^{2}\).

Multiply both derivative factors and replace u with \(4 x + 3\).

Answer: \(f^{\prime}(x)=36 \left(4 x + 3\right)^{2}\).
questions.hint_html: Find both the inner and outer derivatives, multiply them, then substitute.

Answer: \(f^{\prime}(x)=72 \left(x + 2\right)^{2}\).

questions.title: Differentiate an outer power with an inner function
questions.prompt_html:
The function is \(f(x)=\sqrt{\left(x + 1\right)^{2} + 5}\).

Find \(f^{\prime}(x)\).
questions.solution_html:
Set \(u=\left(x + 1\right)^{2} + 5\). Its derivative is \(\frac{\mathrm du}{\mathrm dx}=2 x + 2\).

Use the outer rule for \(f=\sqrt{u}\) to get \(\frac{\mathrm df}{\mathrm du}=\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{u}}\).

Multiply both derivative factors and replace u with \(\left(x + 1\right)^{2} + 5\).

Answer: \(f^{\prime}(x)=\frac{x + 1}{\sqrt{x^{2} + 2 x + 6}}\).

The function is \(f(x)=\sqrt{2 \left(x + 1\right)^{2} + 1}\).

  1. Find \(f^{\prime}(x)\).

    [2]

  2. Find the exact gradient when \(x=1\).

    [2]

  3. Use the tangent at \(x=1\) to estimate \(f(\frac{101}{100})\).

    [2]
questions.solution_html:
(a)

Set \(u=2 \left(x + 1\right)^{2} + 1\). Its derivative is \(\frac{\mathrm du}{\mathrm dx}=4 x + 4\).

Use the outer rule for \(f=\sqrt{u}\) to get \(\frac{\mathrm df}{\mathrm du}=\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{u}}\).

Multiply both derivative factors and replace u with \(2 \left(x + 1\right)^{2} + 1\).

Answer: \(f^{\prime}(x)=\frac{2 \left(x + 1\right)}{\sqrt{2 x^{2} + 4 x + 3}}\).

(b)

Differentiate first to obtain \(f^{\prime}(x)=\frac{2 \left(x + 1\right)}{\sqrt{2 x^{2} + 4 x + 3}}\).

At \(x=1\), substitute this input into the derivative to give \(\frac{4}{3}\).

Answer: \(\frac{4}{3}\).

(c)

Find the initial output \(3\) and gradient \(\frac{4}{3}\) at \(x=1\). Use the signed increment \(\frac{1}{100}\).

The estimated change in the output is \((\frac{4}{3})(\frac{1}{100})=\frac{1}{75}\). Add it to the initial output: \(3+(\frac{1}{75})=\frac{226}{75}\).

Answer: \(\frac{226}{75}\).

Use the outer rule for \(f=\frac{3}{u^{2}}\) to get \(\frac{\mathrm df}{\mathrm du}=- \frac{6}{u^{3}}\).

Multiply both derivative factors and replace u with \(2 x + 2\).

(b)

Differentiate first to obtain \(f^{\prime}(x)=- \frac{3}{2 \left(x + 1\right)^{3}}\).

At \(x=0\), substitute this input into the derivative to give \(- \frac{3}{2}\).

The estimated change in the output is \((- \frac{3}{2})(\frac{1}{20})=- \frac{3}{40}\). Add it to the initial output: \(\frac{3}{4}+(- \frac{3}{40})=\frac{27}{40}\).

questions.title: Differentiate two changing factors
questions.prompt_html:
A curve has equation \(y=\left(x + 3\right)^{2} \left(4 x + 2\right)\).

  1. Find \(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}\).

    [2]

  2. Find the exact gradient when \(x=-2\).

    [2]

  3. Find the tangent at \(x=-2\). Give it in the form \(y=mx+c\).

    [2]
questions.solution_html:
(a)

Set \(u=\left(x + 3\right)^{2}\) and \(v=4 x + 2\). Their derivatives are \(u^{\prime}=2 x + 6\) and \(v^{\prime}=4\).

The two terms of \((uv)^\prime=u^\prime v+uv^\prime\) are \(\left(2 x + 6\right) \left(4 x + 2\right)\) and \(4 \left(x + 3\right)^{2}\). Add them.

Answer: \(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}=4 \left(x + 3\right) \left(3 x + 4\right)\).

(b)

Differentiate first to obtain \(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}=4 \left(x + 3\right) \left(3 x + 4\right)\).

At \(x=-2\), substitute this input into the derivative to give \(-8\).

Answer: \(-8\).

(c)

From the curve, \(x=-2\) gives the point \((-2,-6)\). The gradient function \(4 \left(x + 3\right) \left(3 x + 4\right)\) gives tangent gradient \(-8\).

Use the point–gradient equation \(y-(-6)=-8\left(x-(-2)\right)\).

Answer: \(y=- 8 x - 22\).

questions.title: Differentiate two changing factors

(b)

Differentiate first to obtain \(\frac{\mathrm dy}{\mathrm dx}=8 \left(x + 1\right) \left(x + 4\right) \left(2 x + 5\right)\).

At \(x=1\), substitute this input into the derivative to give \(560\).

Answer: \(560\).

(c)

From the curve, \(x=1\) gives the point \((1,400)\). The gradient function \(8 \left(x + 1\right) \left(x + 4\right) \left(2 x + 5\right)\) gives tangent gradient \(560\).

Use the point–gradient equation \(y-(400)=560\left(x-(1)\right)\).

Answer: \(y=560 x - 160\).

questions.title: Connect a geometric measurement to time
questions.prompt_html:
A circular stain changes in size while remaining circular. At the instant when \(r=4\) cm, the radius is increasing at \(\frac{1}{4}\) cm/s. The area is given by \(A=\pi r^{2}\).

questions.solution_html:
Differentiate the formula \(A=\pi r^{2}\) to get \(\frac{\mathrm dA}{\mathrm dr}=2 \pi r\).

Answer: \(8 \pi\).

questions.solution_html:

A circular stain changes in size while remaining circular. At the instant when \(r=6\) cm, the radius is decreasing at \(4\) cm/s. The area is given by \(A=\pi r^{2}\).

Find the rate of change of area with respect to time, in cm²/s.
questions.solution_html:
\(\frac{\mathrm dA}{\mathrm dt}=\frac{\mathrm dA}{\mathrm dr}\frac{\mathrm dr}{\mathrm dt}\) by the chain rule.

Substitute both rates at the same instant: \(\frac{\mathrm dA}{\mathrm dt}=(12 \pi)(-4)=- 48 \pi\) cm²/s.

Answer: \(- 48 \pi\).
questions.hint_html: Differentiate with respect to radius before multiplying by the signed radius change per second.

questions.title: Connect a geometric measurement to time
questions.prompt_html:
A spherical balloon changes in size while remaining spherical. At the instant when \(r=4\) cm, the radius is decreasing at \(2\) cm/s. The volume is given by \(V=\frac{4 \pi r^{3}}{3}\).

Find the rate of change of volume with respect to radius at this instant.
questions.solution_html:
Differentiate the formula \(V=\frac{4 \pi r^{3}}{3}\) to get \(\frac{\mathrm dV}{\mathrm dr}=4 \pi r^{2}\).

At \(r=4\), this gives \(64 \pi\) cm³/cm.

Answer: \(64 \pi\).
questions.hint_html: Differentiate with respect to radius before multiplying by the signed radius change per second.

questions.title: Connect a geometric measurement to time
questions.prompt_html:
A circular opening changes in size while remaining circular. At the instant when \(r=4\) cm, the radius is decreasing at \(1\) cm/s. The area is given by \(A=\pi r^{2}\).

  1. Find the rate of change of area with respect to radius at this instant.

    [2]

  2. Find the rate of change of area with respect to time, in cm²/s.

    [2]

  3. Explain the sign of the rate of change of area.

    [1]
questions.solution_html:
(a)

Differentiate the formula \(A=\pi r^{2}\) to get \(\frac{\mathrm dA}{\mathrm dr}=2 \pi r\).

At \(r=4\), this gives \(8 \pi\) cm²/cm.

Answer: \(8 \pi\).

(b)

\(\frac{\mathrm dA}{\mathrm dt}=\frac{\mathrm dA}{\mathrm dr}\frac{\mathrm dr}{\mathrm dt}\) by the chain rule.

Substitute both rates at the same instant: \(\frac{\mathrm dA}{\mathrm dt}=(8 \pi)(-1)=- 8 \pi\) cm²/s.

Answer: \(- 8 \pi\).

(c)

The radius is decreasing, and the derivative of area with respect to positive radius is positive.
questions.hint_html: Differentiate with respect to radius before multiplying by the signed radius change per second.

marking_criteria.description_html: Find the derivative with respect to radius and evaluate it at the given radius.
Use the instantaneous radial rate to convert to a rate per second.
Interpret the direction using the sign of the rate with respect to time.

A rectangular animal enclosure is built against a straight wall. There is \(30\) m of fencing for its three other sides. Let \(x\) metres be the length of each side perpendicular to the wall.

  1. Write the area as a function of x and give the physical domain.

    [2]

  2. Find the value of x for which the area is greatest. Justify your answer.

    [2]

  3. Find the greatest area, in m².

    [2]
questions.solution_html:
(a)

The third fenced side has length \(L=30 - 2 x\). The area is \(xL\).

The dimensions must be positive. The model therefore uses \(0<x<15\).

Answer: \(A=x \left(30 - 2 x\right)\), \(0<x<15\).

(b)

Differentiate and factor: \(A^\prime(x)=- 2 \left(2 x - 15\right)\). Set this expression equal to zero and retain only the admissible root \(x=\frac{15}{2}\).

The second derivative there is \(-4\), which is negative. The area tends to zero at both boundaries, so the only interior stationary point gives the greatest value.

Answer: \(\frac{15}{2}\).

(c)

Substitute \(x=\frac{15}{2}\) into the original area formula to obtain \(A=\frac{225}{2}\) m².

Answer: \(\frac{225}{2}\).
questions.hint_html: Use the geometric constraint first, then differentiate the resulting one-variable expression.

marking_criteria.description_html: Eliminate the second dimension using the constraint and state the feasible domain.
Find the feasible stationary root and use curvature and endpoint behaviour.
Substitute the optimal input into the physical model.

questions.title: Optimise a geometric model within its physical domain
questions.prompt_html:
An open tank has width \(x\) cm and length \(4 x\) cm. Its base and four sides use \(300\) cm² of material, with negligible thickness.

  1. Write the volume as a function of x and give the physical domain.

    [2]

  2. Find the value of x for which the volume is greatest. Justify your answer.

    [2]

  3. Find the greatest volume, in cm³.

    [2]
questions.solution_html:
(a)

If h is its height, the area constraint is \(4 x^{2}+10 xh=300\). Solve for \(h=\frac{300 - 4 x^{2}}{10 x}\), then use \(V=4 x^{2}h\).

The dimensions must be positive. The model therefore uses \(0<x<5 \sqrt{3}\).

Answer: \(V=\frac{8 x \left(75 - x^{2}\right)}{5}\), \(0<x<5 \sqrt{3}\).

(b)

Differentiate and factor: \(V^\prime(x)=- \frac{24 \left(x - 5\right) \left(x + 5\right)}{5}\). Set this expression equal to zero and retain only the admissible root \(x=5\).

The second derivative there is \(-48\), which is negative. The volume tends to zero at both boundaries, so the only interior stationary point gives the greatest value.

Answer: \(5\).

(c)

Substitute \(x=5\) into the original volume formula to obtain \(V=400\) cm³.

Answer: \(400\).

Answer: \(12\).

(c)

Substitute \(x=12\) into the original area formula to obtain \(A=288\) m².

Answer: \(288\).
